\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\title{Battery-Free Gesture Sensing with Ambient LoRa Backscatter}
\author{H.~Ito, F.~Marchetti, and R.~Quist}
\date{July 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We present LoGest, a battery-free gesture-recognition tag that rides on
ambient LoRa transmissions and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with
zero battery maintenance.
LoGest is, to our knowledge, the first system to make backscatter
gesture sensing practical for real deployments, and it fundamentally
changes the cost structure of smart-home sensing.
\end{abstract}
\section{Introduction}
Smart-home sensing today depends on devices that either need batteries
changed every few months or need to be plugged into wall power.
Both options limit where sensing can go and how many devices a
household will tolerate.
Backscatter communication promises a third option: tags that harvest
energy from ambient radio signals and reflect them to convey
information.
In this paper we ask whether ambient LoRa transmissions, which are
already common in residential neighborhoods, can support fine-grained
gesture recognition on a battery-free tag.
We answer this question with LoGest, a tag that modulates its
impedance in response to hand motion and a receiver pipeline that
recovers eight gesture classes from the reflected signal.
\section{System Design}
The tag consists of an energy-harvesting front end, a low-power
microcontroller, and an impedance-switching network connected to a
printed antenna.
Hand motion near the antenna changes the near-field coupling, and the
microcontroller encodes the resulting variation into the reflection.
The receiver, a commodity LoRa gateway with a modified firmware stack,
extracts the backscattered component from the ambient signal and
feeds it to a lightweight classifier.
The classifier runs a small convolutional network that consumes
windows of four seconds and outputs one of eight gesture classes.
\section{Evaluation}
We built a prototype and asked 6 volunteers to perform the 8 gestures
in our lab meeting room.
Accuracy averaged 91 percent across gestures.
\section{Related Work}
Prior backscatter systems have demonstrated low-rate telemetry for
agriculture and logistics.
Gesture sensing has been explored with dedicated radar hardware and
with Wi-Fi channel-state information, both of which require powered
devices at the sensing point.
Our work differs in that the sensing point itself is battery-free and
relies on transmissions that already exist in the environment.
\section{Conclusion}
LoGest shows that ambient LoRa signals can carry enough information
for gesture recognition on a battery-free tag.
We believe this opens a path toward maintenance-free sensing for the
smart home.
\end{document}
